{{nihongo||豊受大神宮|'''{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}'''}} is a shrine to to {{ill|Toyouke-hime|en|Toyouke-hime|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyoukebime}} the food goddess located in [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. it is also colloquially known as {{nihongo||外宮|'''{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|lt=Gekū|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}'''|lit. outer shrine}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Outer Shrine (Geku) |url=https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4311.html |access-date=2023-05-05 |website=www.japan-guide.com |language=en}}</ref> In pilgrimage customs people traditionally visit this shrine first and then {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|zh|皇大神宮|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} which is located 4 km to the south<ref name=":0" />

The shrine was founded after [[:en:Emperor Yuryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] dreamt that he saw [[Amaterasu]]. She said she was unable to get food and asked him to bring {{ill|Toyouke-hime|en|Toyouke-hime|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-hime}} from {{ill|Tanba Province|en|Tanba Province|qid=Q954511|lt=Tanba}} help her with food.<ref>https://archive.is/3h7o</ref>

'''Toyouke Daijingu''' (豊受大神宮), also known as the '''Outer Shrine''' (外宮, Gekū), is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Toyokawachō|ja|豊川町 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokawa Town (Ise)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17223204}}, {{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise City}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}. It is one of the two main shrines of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}} and is classified as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Grand Shrine).
== Overview ==
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, also commonly referred to as Gekū (外宮), is one of the two main shrines of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}, located in {{ill|Toyokawachō|ja|豊川町 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokawa-chō, Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17223204}}, [[:en:Ise City|Ise City]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}. This shrine venerates {{ill|Toyouke-hime|en|Toyouke-hime|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-Ōmikami}}, the deity of food, clothing, and shelter. The shrine is said to have been established during the 22nd year of the reign of Emperor Yūryaku and is built in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Yuiitsu-Shimmei-zukuri}} architectural style.

== location ==
Gekū is located approximately 5–6 minutes' walk from {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise-shi Station}} via the {{ill|Gekū Sando|ja|外宮参道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Outer Shrine Path|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q42387615}}. It is customary to visit Gekū before proceeding to {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|lt=Kōtai Jingū|lt=Kōtai Jingu (Naikū)|ja|皇大神宮 (内宮)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingu (Naikū)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the inner shrine.

== Shrine Grounds ==
Gekū is surrounded by ancient trees, such as the "Kiyomori Kusunoki" (清盛楠), named after [[Taira no Kiyomori]]{{citation needed |Taira no Kiyomori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira no Kiyomori}}, and features a beautiful magatama-shaped pond where Mie Prefecture's flower, the iris, blooms in summer. 

The shrine buildings are surrounded by four layers of fencing—Itagaki, Sototamagaki, Uchi-tamagaki, and Mizugaki—and are guarded and maintained 24/7 by Jingu guards. Gekū’s divine blessing is believed to offer protection for industries and the blessings of food, clothing, and shelter.

== Overview ==
Located in the city center of {{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise, Mie}}, '''Gekū''' (外宮) is about a 5-6 minute walk from {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise Station}}, accessible via the {{ill|Gekū Sando|ja|外宮参道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gekū Sando}} from {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|en|Central Japan Railway Company|qid=Q513679|lt=JR Central}} and {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|en|Kintetsu Railway|qid=Q1531085|lt=Kintetsu Railway}}.<ref>Edited by Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.32</ref> Together with the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Naikū), it forms the '''Shōgū''' (正宮). Traditionally, it has been customary to visit Gekū before proceeding to Naikū when worshipping at the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}.<ref name="ub8">Edited by Ise Bunka-sha (2009): p.98</ref> This practice is known as the "Gekū Senrei no Rei" (外宮先祭の礼).<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|和書 |title=偽書が揺るがせた日本史 |date=2020/3/25 |publisher=（株）山川出版社 |page=82-84 |author=原田　実}}</ref>

Despite its central location, the shrine grounds retain a tranquil, otherworldly atmosphere. Notable features include the ancient "'''Kiyomori Kusu'''" (清盛楠), a sacred camphor tree said to have brushed against the crown of [[Taira no Kiyomori]]{{citation needed |Taira no Kiyomori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira no Kiyomori}} when he visited the shrine as an imperial envoy (勅使),<ref name="ub8" /> and the "'''Magatama Pond'''" (勾玉池), where {{ill|Acorus calamus|en|Acorus calamus|qid=Q158008|lt=Acorus calamus}}—Mie Prefecture’s official flower—bloom in early summer.<ref name="ub9">Edited by Ise Bunka-sha (2009): p.99</ref>

Outside the shrine, the {{ill|Central business district|en|Central business district|qid=Q738570|lt=central business district}} (CBD) of Ise extends into {{ill|Honmachi|ja|本町 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honmachi, Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11520676}}, a historic torii-front town where the {{ill|Ise City Tourism Association|ja|伊勢市観光協会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Tourism Association|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} has its headquarters. The surrounding area, including Gekū Sando and the station-front streets, is a mix of {{ill|Omiyage|ja|土産物|Omiyage=Omiyage|lt=souvenir shops|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omiyage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 土産|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q63224833}}, {{ill|Ryokan|en|Ryokan|qid=Q562930|lt=ryokan}}, {{ill|Bank|en|Bank|qid=Q22687|lt=banks}}, and branch offices of major {{ill|Business sector|en|Business sector|qid=Q3477367|lt=corporations}}.

The shrine buildings, like those of Kōtai Jingū, are enclosed within four layers of fences: '''Itagaki''' (板垣), '''Sototamagaki''' (外玉垣), '''Uchitamagaki''' (内玉垣), and '''Mizugaki''' (瑞垣). Guardhouses (宿衛屋) are stationed at the north and south gates. The shrine is patrolled and maintained 24/7 by the {{ill|Jingū Guards|ja|神宮衛士|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Guards}}, who work in rotating shifts.<ref>『一般人は入れない立入禁止地帯』, History Mystery Research Group, {{ill|Saizusha Corporation|ja|彩図社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saizusha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11487991}}, 2011</ref>

Regarding divine virtues (神徳), in the doctrine of {{ill|Ise faith|lt=Ise faith|lt=Ise Shintō|ja|伊勢神道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Shintō}}, as written in the {{ill|Shintō Gobusho|ja|神道五部書|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shintō Gobusho}}, the enshrined deity, {{ill|Toyouke-hime|en|Toyouke-hime|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-hime}}, is regarded as the deity of all creation and is considered synonymous with the primordial deities {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}} and {{ill|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|en|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|qid=Q478504|lt=Kuni-no-Tokotachi}}.<ref name=":0" /> However, the modern {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|qid=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines}} does not adopt this interpretation, instead defining Toyouke-Ōmikami (豊受大御神) as the guardian deity of industry, who bestows blessings related to rice, clothing, food, and shelter.<ref>Signboard before the Hiyoke Bridge</ref>

== Deities Enshrined ==

; Main Deity
* '''{{ill|Toyouke-hime|en|Toyouke-hime|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-Ōmikami}}''' (とようけのおおみかみ)
: According to the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', the divine object (*goshintai*, 御神体) enshrined here is the *Shinkyōtsukagami* (真経津鏡).

; Auxiliary Deities
: Three *Mitomo-no-Kami* (御伴神) are enshrined in the same sanctuary (*Aiden-shin*, 相殿神), with one deity positioned in the east and two in the west.<ref name="as28">Mitsuhashi (2013): p.128</ref> Some interpretations identify these three deities as:
* '''{{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|en|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ame-no-Hikohikoho-no-Ninigi}}''' (天津彦彦火瓊瓊杵尊, あまつひこひこほににぎのみこと)
* '''{{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|Ame-no-Koyane|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane}}''' (天児屋根命, あめのこやねのみこと)
* '''{{ill|Futodama|en|Futodama|qid=Q11059539|lt=Futodama}}''' (太玉命, ふとだま)
<ref name="as28" />

== History ==

=== History ===
Gekū’s origin is not recorded in the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} or {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}. According to the shrine’s own records, the shrine was established following a divine revelation to Emperor Yūryaku by {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu-Ōmikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q455602}}, who expressed the need for a deity to assist with meals. Toyouke-Ōmikami was then invited from {{ill|Tanba Province|en|Tanba Province|qid=Q954511|lt=Tanba Province}} to the "Yamada Plain" near Naikū.
=== History ===
In Japanese mythology {{ill|Toyouke-hime|en|Toyouke-hime|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-hime}} was either killed by [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Efn|In the [[Nihon Shoki]]}}<ref name="Roberts 2010">{{cite book|last=Roberts|first=Jeremy|url=http://www.enryo.ro/carti/Japanese%20mythology%20A%20to%20Z.pdf|title=Japanese Mythology A To Z|publisher=Chelsea House Publishers|year=2010|isbn=978-1-60413-435-3|edition=2nd|location=New York}}</ref> or by [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]]{{Efn|In the [[Kojiki]]}}. Amaterasu mourned the death of her and in the [[Nihon Shoki]] the reason the sun and the moon are on opposite sides of the sky is that Amaterasu was unwilling to go near [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] the moon god after he committed the murder.<ref name="Roberts 2010" /> Amaterasu is linked with Toyouke-hime as the sun is necessary for food to grow. This was prior to the [[:en:Tenson Korin|Tenson Korin]] and the establishment of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]]. {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}} is said to have established the shrine to worship [[Amaterasu]] at a permanent location after many temporary locations.{{sfn|Bocking|2013|p=51}} In contrast with {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|lt=|ja|皇大神宮|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotai jingu|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, this shrine is not explicitly mentioned in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki]]. 

Besides the traditional establishment date of 4 BC,<ref>''Encyclopædia Britannica{{Snd}} Ise Shrine'' https://www.britannica.com/ebc/article-9368233</ref> it has also been proposed as having been made in the 5th century.<ref name="witcombe.sbc.edu">''Sacred Places{{Snd}} Ise Shrine'' http://witcombe.sbc.edu/sacredplaces/ise.html</ref> The shrine officially states it was created 1500 years ago in response to a revelation from [[Amaterasu]] that the shrine was needed.<ref>{{Cite web|title=About Ise Jingu｜Ise Jingu|url=https://www.isejingu.or.jp/en/about/index.html|access-date=2023-05-05|website=Ise Jingu|language=en}}</ref>

The shrine has been traditionally rebuilt every 20 years.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ise Jingu - Geku (Toyouke Daijingu) {{!}} Sightseeing Spots MIE(Ise-Shima) {{!}} Kintetsu Railway Co.,Ltd.|url=https://www.kintetsu.co.jp/foreign/english/sightseeing/mie/spot02.html|access-date=2023-05-05|website=www.kintetsu.co.jp}}</ref> 

There is a separate shrine dedicated to Toyouke's [[Mitama#Ara-mitama and nigi-mitama|Ara-mitama]], or {{Nihongo|2=豊受大御神荒魂|3=Toyouke-Ōmikami no Ara-mitama}} called {{ill|Taka-no-Miya|ja|多賀宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takanomiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11431075}} (Takamiya) inside this shrine. 

=== History ===
The origin of the enshrinement of Gekū (*Toyouke Daijingu*) is not mentioned in either the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}'' or the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}''.<ref name="as93">Mitsuhashi (2013): p.93</ref> According to the shrine record ''{{ill|Enryaku Gishikichō|lt=Enryaku Gishikichō|lt=Toyukegū Gishikichō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyukegū Gishikichō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延暦儀式帳}}'', compiled in 804 (*Enryaku* 23), {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q455602}} (the enshrined deity of ''{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}'' or *Naikū*) appeared in a dream of ''{{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|en|Emperor Yūryaku|qid=Q357235|lt=Emperor Yūryaku}}''<ref name="as93" /> and revealed, "I cannot dine in peace alone. Summon *Toyouke-Ōkami* from *Tanba Province* to be near me." Although *Toyukegū Gishikichō* does not specify the year, ''{{ill|Daijingū Shozatsujiki|ja|大神宮諸雑事記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijingū Shozatsujiki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' states that this event occurred in "the 21st year of Emperor Yūryaku, *Hinoto-mi* (丁巳),"<ref name="as94">Mitsuhashi (2013): p.94</ref> which corresponds to Yūryaku 21. In response to this divine oracle, on the 7th day of the 7th month (lunar calendar) of Yūryaku 22, *Toyouke Ōmikami* was enshrined in *"Yamada-no-hara, Numaki-no-sato, Watarai District, Ise Province"*, near Naikū.<ref name="as94" /> 

The record states that the enshrinement of Gekū occurred 484 years after Naikū, but when mechanically calculating this duration based on historical reigns<ref>{{see|List of ancient Japanese emperors' reigns and their corresponding Western years}}</ref>, the years do not match exactly.<ref name="as94" /> In the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}'', the shrine is listed as *Watarai-no-miya, Four Shrines* (*度会宮 四座*), classified as a major shrine.

The ''{{ill|Watarai clan|ja|度会氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai clan}}'' served as hereditary shrine priests (*Shinkan*, 神職) for generations. During the *Kamakura period*, some shrine priests at Gekū began advocating that Gekū should be regarded as equal to or even superior in Rank to Naikū. Around 1296 or 1297, Gekū started using the title *"Toyouke Kōdaigū"*, which included the imperial character (*皇*, Kō), prompting protests from Naikū.<ref name=":0" /> Against this backdrop, ''{{ill|Watarai Ieyuki|ja|度会家行|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai Ieyuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11486121}}'' formulated the doctrine of ''{{ill|Ise faith|lt=Ise faith|lt=Ise Shintō|ja|伊勢神道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Shintō}}'' (Watarai Shintō), asserting that *Toyouke Ōmikami* was identical to {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}} and {{ill|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|ja|国常立神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuni-no-Tokotachi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国之常立神}}, thus making Gekū superior to Naikū. Meanwhile, the shrine town of ''{{ill|Yamada|ja|山田 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada, Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11470062}}'' developed around Gekū.

=== Meiji Era and Beyond ===
During the ''{{ill|Ise Riot|ja|伊勢暴動|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Riot|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379085}}'' of 1876, fires broke out in the towns of Nakajima, Uraguchi, Tokiwa, and Ōseko. Although Gekū took defensive measures, it escaped destruction and arson.<ref>Kaneko (1983): pp.214-215</ref> On January 14, 1945, at 2:53 PM,<ref name="ss9">Nihon no Kūshū Henshū Iinkai (1980): p.239</ref> six bombs were dropped within the sacred grounds of Gekū, damaging the *Gojōden* (五丈殿), *Kyūjōden* (九丈殿), *Kaguraden* (神楽殿), and *Saikan* (斎館).<ref name="yk">Nishigaki & Matsushima (1974): p.247</ref> However, the damage was relatively minor, with only eaves, sliding doors, and fences sustaining damage, along with a few holes in the roofs.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|author=Nakamura Hisanori|url=http://www.asahi.com/area/mie/articles/MTW20120818251060001.html|title=[5] Exaggerated Reports for Wartime Propaganda|work={{ill|Asahi Shimbun Digital|ja|朝日新聞デジタル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asahi Shimbun Digital|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 朝日新聞 (ニュースサイト)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11517520}}|publisher={{ill|The Asahi Shimbun|en|The Asahi Shimbun|qid=Q720503|lt=Asahi Shimbun}}|date=2012-08-18|accessdate=2015-01-25|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150125095304/http://www.asahi.com/area/mie/articles/MTW20120818251060001.html|archivedate=2015-01-25}}</ref>

During the ''{{ill|Ujiyamada Air Raid|ja|宇治山田空襲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ujiyamada Air Raid}}'' on July 28-29, incendiary bombs fell inside the sacred enclosure (*Mikakiuchi*, 御垣内), but the shrine itself was not engulfed in flames.<ref name="kg4">Yano (2006): p.184</ref> The aftermath revealed that the debris of incendiary bombs collected from the shrine grounds filled three truckloads.<ref name="kg4" />

== Grounds ==
The main shrine consists of three buildings: the Main Sanctuary (正殿), the Western Treasure Hall (西宝殿), and the Eastern Treasure Hall (東宝殿).<ref name="ub9" /> These are surrounded by multiple layers of wooden fences, making them not directly visible from the worship area. Behind the Main Sanctuary are the Mikeden (御饌殿) and the Geheiden (外幣殿).<ref name="ub9" /> Next to the main shrine is the sacred site (御敷地) where the shrine will be rebuilt in the next {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|神宮式年遷宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Shikinen Sengū}}.<ref name="ub9" /> This site, known as the "Old Shrine Site" (古殿地), was where the previous shrine stood before the last relocation.

The shrine grounds are about one-tenth the size of the Inner Shrine and feature left-side traffic, unlike the Inner Shrine.<ref>矢野（2006）：46 - 47ページ</ref> Within the grounds, there are three subsidiary shrines of high Rank: {{ill|Taka-no-Miya|ja|多賀宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takanomiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11431075}}, {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|ja|風宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaze-no-Miya}}, and {{ill|Tsuchi-no-Miya|ja|土宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchi-no-Miya}}, along with buildings such as the purification hall (斎館), the Kagura Hall (神楽殿), the sacred fire hall (忌火屋殿) for preparing offerings, and the Sake Storage Hall (御酒殿). The boundary of the shrine is guarded by the {{ill|Miyanomeguri-no-Kami|ja|四至神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyanomeguri-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyanomeguri-no-Kami}}.<ref name="ub8" /><ref>矢野（2006）：47ページ</ref>

A road extending northwest from the North Gate Torii leads to the {{ill|Watarai Kunimi Shrine|lt=Watarai Kunimi Shrine|lt=Watarai-koku Gokami Shrine|ja|度会国御神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai-koku Gokami Shrine}}, which enshrines the guardian deities of Ise City and the Watarai District. Further along is {{ill|Ōtsu Shrine (Ise)|ja|大津神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtsu Shrine (Ise)}}, protecting the mouth of the {{ill|Isuzu River|en|Isuzu River|qid=Q6089522|lt=Isuzu River}}.<ref name="ub9" /> Additionally, some shrines within the precincts, such as {{ill|Watarai Okunitama-hime Shrine|lt=Watarai Okunitama-hime Shrine|lt=Watarai Ōkunidama-hime Shrine|ja|度会大国玉比賣神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai Ōkunidama-hime Shrine}} and {{ill|Igari Shrine|ja|伊我理神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Igari Shrine}}, are not directly connected by paths and require exiting onto the Mikumoto Road (三重県道32号伊勢磯部線) to access.<ref>伊勢文化舎（2008）：37ページ</ref>

=== Daiichi-torii-guchi Sando ===
Daiichi-torii-guchi Sando is the primary route into the shrine. It starts at the Hiyokebashi bridge entrance, and beyond this bridge, the Temizusha (ablution font) is visible on the left side.<ref name=":0" />

=== Temizusha ===
A {{ill|Chōzuya|en|Chōzuya|qid=Q1069667|lt=Temizusha}} is present at the shrine for worshippers to purify .<ref name=":0" />

=== Kitamikado-guchi Sando ===
An alternative {{ill|Sandō|en|Sandō|qid=Q667783|lt=entrance path}} for the shrine.<ref name=":0" />

=== Saikan and Anzaisho ===
Saikan and Anzaisho are the Purification Hall and Hall for Imperial Household Visitors respectively. They are on the right side of the pilgrimage path. The Saikan, which is surrounded by fences, is used by Shinto priests to purify themselves. They stay here for one or two nights to cleanse their minds from worldly concerns before performing rituals, as they bathe and eat meals prepared with sacred fire to achieve spiritual serenity; adjacent to Saikan, there is a building called Anzaisho, which serves as the Hall for the Emperor and Empress.<ref name=":0" />

=== Kaguraden ===
There is a large [[:en:Kaguraden|Kaguraden]] at Geku.<ref name=":0" />

=== Honden ===
Toyouke Omikami is enshrined at the Honden. It lies in the most sacred area enclosed by four rows of fences, and the structure remains unchanged from 1500 years ago. Worshippers can only approach the first gate.<ref name=":0" />

== Shrines Associated with the Outer Shrine (Gekū) ==

=== Gekū Sessha (Outer Shrine Subordinate Shrines) ===
''Sessha'' (摂社) are shrines listed in the ''Engishiki Jinmyōchō'' (延喜式神名帳) that are neither ''shōgū'' nor ''betsugū''. By definition, all ''sessha'' are ''shikinaisha'' (式内社). However, most were abandoned during the Sengoku period and only revived between the early Edo period (1630s) and the Meiji period (1870s). Consequently, they are often considered probable sites of ''shikinaisha''.<ref>{{ill|Katsunoshin Sakurai|ja|櫻井勝之進|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsunoshin Sakurai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11544758}}, ''Ise Jingū''.</ref> There are 16 ''sessha''.

== Festivals ==
Rituals at {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}} follow the principle of "Gekū-saki-matsuri" (外宮先祭), meaning that ceremonies are conducted at {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōyuke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Gekū, the Outer Shrine) before those at {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Naikū, the Inner Shrine). However, during the {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|神宮式年遷宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Shikinen Sengū}}, Naikū is prioritized.<ref name="sk">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai, ed. (1990): p. 150</ref>

=== Daily Morning and Evening Great Food Offerings Ceremony ===
The '''Higoto-Asayu-Ōmiketsai''' (日別朝夕大御饌祭) is performed twice daily, with the '''Morning Ōmiketsai''' held from 8:00 AM to 9:00 AM and the '''Evening Ōmiketsai''' from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM at the Gekū Mikeden (Outer Shrine Food Hall). This ceremony involves offering sacred food ([[御饌]]) to the deities.<ref name="sk" /> It is also referred to as the '''Jōten-Ōmike''' (常典御饌).

A {{ill|Kannushi|ja|権禰宜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gon-negi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神職|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q60523}} who has undergone purification at the Tōyuke Daijingū Saikan (斎館) prepares the offerings. Sacred fire (忌火) is ignited at the shrine's {{ill|Imibiya-den|ja|忌火屋殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imibiya-den|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} using a traditional fire drill. A purified [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto priest]] prepares food offerings, including three servings of rice (御飯, onii), water from {{ill|Kami-no-Mii Shrine|ja|上御井神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-no-Mii Shrine}}, salt (御塩, mishio), dried sea bream (or seasonal items such as dried squid, barracuda, or gnomefish), dried bonito, seaweed, vegetables, fruits, and three offerings of sacred sake (清酒). These are then presented by one {{ill|Negi|ja|禰宜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Negi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11594490}}, one {{ill|Kannushi|ja|権禰宜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gon-negi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神職|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q60523}}, one {{ill|Miya-zukasa|ja|宮掌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miya-zukasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and two attendants at the Mikeden, dedicated to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu-Ōmikami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q455602}}, {{ill|Toyouke-hime|ja|豊受大御神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōyuke-Ōmikami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to トヨウケビメ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2983724}}, {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|ja|天手力男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Tajikarao|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノタヂカラオ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q849412}}, and {{ill|Takuhadachiji-hime|en|Takuhadachiji-hime|qid=Q11110848|lt=Takuhadachiji-hime}}, as well as three accompanying deities.<ref name="sk" />

Salt used as a food offering is sourced from the {{ill|Mishioden Shrine|ja|御塩殿神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishioden Shrine}} and transported along the designated {{ill|Mishio Path|ja|御塩道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishio Path|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The transport is carried out via the "Mishio Bridge" (御塩橋), a structure used exclusively for this purpose within the shrine grounds.

Rice is cultivated at the "Jingū Shinden" (神宮神田) within Ise City, and vegetables are grown at the "Jingū Misono" (神宮御園). The shrine adheres to a principle of self-sufficiency for food offerings, with ceremonial earthenware (土器) crafted at the shrine's ceramic production site in {{ill|Q11240358|ja|明和町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiwa, Mie|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11240358}} within {{ill|Taki District, Mie|en|Taki District, Mie|qid=Q1042360|lt=Taki District, Mie}}.<ref name="sk" />

== Sacred Horses (Shinme) ==
[[File:Shinme(Geku)02.jpg|thumb|Appearance of a sacred horse<ref>[http://www.jingukaikan.jp/kaikan/tsuitachi.html 『月の初めはお伊勢さんで　朔日参りのご案内』神宮会館] Retrieved April 22, 2015.</ref>]]

At the {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|外宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Outer Shrine (Gekū)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 豊受大神宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11633343}}, two {{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sacred horses|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11591047}} donated by the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|qid=Q909452|lt=Imperial Household of Japan}} are kept.<ref name="jp">JTB Publishing (2011): p.140</ref> However, if one of the sacred horses passes away, there will be a period when only one remains until a new one is donated. Deceased sacred horses are buried in a designated grave, and a formal '''horse dedication ceremony (牽進式, Kenshinshiki)''' is held for newly donated horses. After undergoing purification, the new sacred horse is led inside the sanctuary of the {{ill|Main Shrine (Seigū)|ja|正宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Main Shrine (Seigū)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, where a [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto priest]] recites a '''norito''' (Shinto prayer) to report the dedication of the horse before the deity.<ref>[http://www.isejingu.or.jp/whatsnew/detail.php?uid=127 『October 1st – Sacred Horse Dedication Ceremony (御馬牽進式, Miuma Kenshinshiki) was conducted』 Ise Jingu] Retrieved April 22, 2015.</ref>

The sacred horses are usually kept in the '''divine stable (御厩, Mi-Uma-ya)''', though they may not always be present depending on the weather or their health.<ref>Publishing Division, Domestic Information Section, Third Editorial Department (2014): p.17</ref> Locals respectfully refer to them as '''"O-Uma-sama" (お馬さま)''', and the horses remain unfazed by photography,<ref>Shufu no Tomosha Editorial Team (2011): pp.24, 81, 87</ref> though flash photography is strictly prohibited.

On the '''1st, 11th, and 21st of every month''', the sacred horses participate in a ritual called '''Shinme Kensan (神馬牽参)''', where they visit the Main Shrine to pay respects.<ref name="jp" /> Around '''8:00 AM''', the sacred horse is led by priests to the front of the Main Shrine and performs a bow before the deity.<ref>Shufu no Tomosha Editorial Team (2011): p.87</ref> However, the ceremony may be canceled in case of rain or if the horse refuses to proceed. During the '''Shinme Kensan''', the horse wears a '''ceremonial horse cloth (馬衣, Uma-ginu)''' adorned with the {{ill|Kikumon (chrysanthemum crests)|ja|菊花紋章|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chrysanthemum Seal|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11082563}}.<ref name="jp" />

The {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|lt=Kōtai Jingū|lt=Inner Shrine (Naikū)|ja|内宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inner Shrine (Naikū)}} also keeps '''two sacred horses''', and they perform the '''Shinme Kensan''' ritual on the same days as the Outer Shrine.<ref name="jp" />

A free parking lot with '''434 spaces''' is available in front of the '''North Gate'''.<ref>Mie Prefecture Tourism Federation 『[http://www.kankomie.or.jp/sagasu12_barrier/barifuri/leisure/area_ise/01-jingu.html Mie Barrier-Free Leisure Guide: Ise-Shima, Okage Yokocho]』</ref>

=== Facilities ===
* '''Sengūkan Museum'''
[[File:Sengukan, Ise Geku.jpg|thumb|Sengūkan Museum]]
:: Opened on '''April 7, 2012''', this museum provides exhibits and information on the '''Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮) relocation ceremony'''.<ref name="hn">"Passing down the significance of Shikinen Sengū to the future – Sengūkan Museum opens April 7" [[Ise-Shima Home News]], March 17, 2012, p.2</ref> Located within the Outer Shrine grounds by '''Magatama Pond''', it showcases models of the Outer Shrine's Main Sanctuary and other areas, alongside theater displays and video presentations.<ref name="hn" /> The '''reinforced concrete building''' consists of '''one above-ground floor and one basement floor''', covering '''2,440 square meters''', with a total construction cost of '''2.5 billion yen'''.<ref name="hn" /><ref name="ik">[[Ise-Shima Keizai Shimbun]] "[http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/1386/ Sengūkan Museum opens—Exhibiting the 'invisible' aspects of Ise Grand Shrine]" April 8, 2012 (accessed June 22, 2012)</ref> The museum also includes a '''rest area''' and a '''dedication stage''' for performances.<ref name="ik" />

:: Since its opening, the museum has attracted an '''average of 2,000 visitors per day''', surpassing expectations and reaching '''50,000 visitors by May 2012'''.<ref>[[Ise Chamber of Commerce]] Women's Division "[http://www.ise-cci.or.jp/josei/2012/05/31/%E3%81%9B%E3%82%93%E3%81%90%E3%81%86%E9%A4%A8%E8%A6%96%E5%AF%9F%E7%A0%94%E4%BF%AE/ Sengūkan Museum Inspection and Training]" May 31, 2012 (accessed June 22, 2012)</ref> By '''August 6, 2012''', the museum surpassed '''100,000 visitors''', contributing to the increase in '''Outer Shrine pilgrimages'''.<ref>Yudai Nakahira "[http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20120807/CK2012080702000013.html Sengūkan Museum surpasses 100,000 visitors]" <[https://megalodon.jp/2012-0830-0923-05/www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20120807/CK2012080702000013.html Web Archive]> {{ill|Chunichi Shimbun|en|Chunichi Shimbun|qid=Q904678|lt=Chunichi Shimbun}}, August 7, 2012 (accessed August 30, 2012)</ref>

:: On '''October 22, 2017''', {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2017)|en|Typhoon Lan (2017)|qid=Q42108577|lt=Typhoon 21}} caused '''Magatama Pond''' to flood, resulting in '''severe water damage'''. The '''underground exhibit room was submerged''', while the '''first-floor exhibition area and office rooms''' sustained flooding, affecting '''electrical and air conditioning systems'''.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://mainichi.jp/articles/20171025/k00/00m/040/048000c|date=October 24, 2017|accessdate=June 30, 2018|title=Typhoon 21 causes flooding at Ise Shrine's Sengūkan Museum|publisher=[[Mainichi Shimbun]]}}</ref> Due to the damage, the museum was forced to '''close for two years''' (though the free rest area remained open during renovations). The restoration included '''wall and floor replacements''', '''waterproofing measures''' such as '''1.2-meter-high flood barriers''' and '''flood doors''' at six key entrances, and the construction of a '''viewing deck with free Wi-Fi''' over '''Magatama Pond'''.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.isenp.co.jp/2019/11/07/38225/|date=November 7, 2019|accessdate=November 10, 2019|title=Sengūkan Museum reopens after two-year closure due to Typhoon damage|publisher=[[Ise Shimbun]]}}</ref> The museum '''reopened on November 7, 2019''', after completing these renovations.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.isenp.co.jp/2019/11/08/38248/|date=November 8, 2019|accessdate=November 10, 2019|title=Sengūkan Museum fully restored – Officials celebrate reopening|publisher=Ise Shimbun}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20191108/CK2019110802000023.html|author=Nobu Takahashi|date=November 8, 2019|accessdate=November 10, 2019|title=Sengūkan Museum reopens – Large crowds cause temporary admission limits|publisher=Chunichi Shimbun}}</ref>

== Deities ==
; Main Deity
* '''{{ill|Toyouke-hime|en|Toyouke-hime|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-Ōmikami}}'''
: According to the {{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chronicle of Princess Yamatohime|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}, the sacred object of worship is the Makufutsukagami mirror.

; Associated Deities
: Known as the "Mitomo no Kami," these three deities are enshrined in the east and west side halls. They include {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|en|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi}}, {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋根命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qid=Q2564508}}, and {{ill|Futodama|en|Futodama|qid=Q11059539|lt=Futodama}}. 

== Rituals ==
Gekū holds daily rituals, including the Morning and Evening Grand Offerings, where sacred food prepared with utmost purity is offered to the deities. These ceremonies are conducted in the Mikeden, a sacred hall dedicated to this purpose.

== Access ==
* '''By Train:''' Approx. 5 minutes' walk from {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise-shi Station}} on the JR Sangu Line or the Kintetsu Yamada Line.
* '''By Bus:''' Disembark at "Gekū-mae" bus stop.
* '''By Car:''' About 5 minutes from the Ise Nishi IC on the Ise Expressway.
